packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (packet-09). Images only; no outside source consulted; no identification of work or author attempted.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- 12 images. image-001 = overview of view 1; image-002..005 = pieces of view 1 (002 top left, 003 top right, 004 bottom left, 005 bottom right); image-006 = overview of view 2; image-007..012 = pieces of view 2 (007 top of second column, 008 top of third column, 009 top of fourth column, 010/011/012 the corresponding bottoms).
- Object: a small parchment bifolium (or two joined pieces) mounted in a modern patterned-paper folder, photographed with a colour target and ruler. View 1 shows it folded: one complete column (left) and, to its right, a second column whose right two thirds are covered by a folded-over flap carrying the line ends of a different column. View 2 shows it opened flat, held by white cord weights: four columns across - a narrow strip at far left (only the right-hand ends of its lines survive), a full column, the gutter, then two more full columns. The cords cover the upper and lower margins and possibly the first/last line.
- Each column has about 31-33 lines inside ruled vertical bounding lines. No running titles visible (upper margin partly covered). No rubricated headings as separate lines.
- Enlarged red initials, 2-3 lines high, with the opening words set beside them: "S" (view 1 left column, image-004), "T" (view 2 fourth column, image-009). Red paragraph marks and red-stroked capitals inside the lines. No underlining; no interlinear or marginal glosses seen. A small pencil stroke/number in the left margin of image-004 (modern).
- Damage: brown staining and abrasion over the top third of the second, third and fourth columns in view 2; the third column's lines 3-8 are almost effaced. Images are lower resolution than a scan (phone-type photographs), which limits minim-level certainty.
- The fourth column of view 2 (image-009/012) is the same text as the flap seen in view 1 (image-003/005 right part): overlapping, not additional text.
- Tentative interpretation only: continuous prose divided into sections, each opened at a red initial by a short quoted clause (LEMMA? below) which the following prose then discusses with formulae such as "S(ed) q(ue)rend(um) est ...", "Et d(icen)d(um) q(uod) ...", "p(rim)o ... s(ecund)o ... t(er)cio ... quarto".

AREAS SELECTED
(1) View 1 left column, whole (image-002, 004).
(2) View 2 fourth column, from the red "T" down (image-009, 012).
(3) View 2 third column, lower two thirds (image-008, 011).
(4) View 2 second column, middle and bottom (image-007, 010).
UNREAD: far-left strip of view 2 (no reading-size crop; only line ends visible); the half-covered second column of view 1 (image-003/005 left part); effaced upper lines of the second, third and fourth columns of view 2.

Conventions: (..) proposed expansion; ? uncertain; [illegible]; 7 = Tironian et.

LIMITATIONS
- Photographs are of modest resolution and taken at an angle; minims and abbreviation strokes are often not resolvable, so several words are read from overall shape. Readings with "?" should be treated as proposals.
- White cords cross the top and bottom margins in view 2 and may hide a first or last line of each column.
- The proper name at image-009 l.13 is transcribed from its letters ("bartholome" + us-sign); I have not interpreted it.
- Column order across the opened bifolium is physical left-to-right only; whether the two leaves are consecutive is not determinable from the images. The far-left strip of view 2 and the half-hidden second column of view 1 are unread.
- Line numbers are counted from the top of each crop; overlaps are flagged and are not additional text.
- Suggested further views: flat, higher-resolution images of each column without the cords; a reading-size crop of the far-left strip in view 2; a crop of the view 1 second column with the flap lifted.
- No exposure to any outside source, catalogue, edition or earlier transcription.
